extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to Elsevier journals (particularly corresponding authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) statement that assigns one or more standardized contributor-role labels to each author, ensuring accuracy and agreement among authors and placement in the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author is responsible for ensuring that the descriptions are accurate and agreed by all authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author must confirm all authors agree with assigned roles before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role(s) of all authors must be listed
rubrics_metrics.description: The role(s) of all authors should be listed, using the relevant above categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each author and assign one or more of the CRediT role labels shown on the page. Use the exact role names from the taxonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors may have multiple roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may have contributed in multiple roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign all applicable roles to each author rather than forcing a single-role choice; roles may be comma-separated in the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT does not change authorship qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT in no way changes the journal’s criteria to qualify for authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The taxonomy documents contributions but does not alter journal policies on who qualifies as an author; authorship criteria remain those of the journal/ICMJE, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT statements should be provided during the submission process and will appear above the acknowledgment section of the published paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the completed CRediT statement when submitting the manuscript (e.g., via Editorial Manager); the publisher will display it in the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas; formulation or evolution of overarching research goals and aims

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Development or design of methodology; creation of models

rubrics_metrics.name: Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification, whether as a part of the activity or separate, of the overall replication/ reproducibility of results/experiments and other research outputs

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of statistical, mathematical, computational, or other formal techniques to analyze or synthesize study data

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting a research and investigation process, specifically performing the experiments, or data/evidence collection

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of study materials, reagents, materials, patients, laboratory samples, animals, instrumentation, computing resources, or other analysis tools

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data (including software code, where it is necessary for interpreting the data itself) for initial use and later reuse

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing - Original Draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically writing the initial draft (including substantive translation)

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing - Review & Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work by those from the original research group, specifically critical review, commentary or revision – including pre-or postpublication stages

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically visualization/ data presentation

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight and leadership responsibility for the research activity planning and execution, including mentorship external to the core team

rubrics_metrics.name: Project administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and coordination responsibility for the research activity planning and execution

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of the financial support for the project leading to this publication

rubrics_metrics.name: Example formatting (sample statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example shows authors listed by name followed by colon and comma-separated CRediT role names (e.g., 'Zhang San: Conceptualization, Methodology, Software').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear, consistent format in the submitted statement; follow publisher/editorial system examples (e.g., Editorial Manager / ScienceDirect examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and further resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxonomy reproduced from Brand et al. (2015) with permission; the page links to further explanatory material and an explainer video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the original Brand et al. (2015) publication and the publisher's explainer materials for implementation details and examples.
